Clues: a multiple of 6; between 271984 and 272040; even; digit sum 12; thousands digit 2. Which of these numbers fits all the clues?

  2. B722010
  3. C272001

Answer & method
Answer D: 272010

272010 fits every clue: a multiple of 6; between 271984 and 272040; even; digit sum 12; thousands digit 2.

StretchFactors and multiples

Which of these has the smallest value?

  1. A5th multiple of 8
  2. BHCF of 14 and 21
  3. CNumber of factors of 18
  4. DLCM of 20 and 30

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Work out the value of each one first, then compare the four numbers.

Answer & method
Answer C: Number of factors of 18

5th multiple of 8 = 40; LCM of 20 and 30 = 60; HCF of 14 and 21 = 7; Number of factors of 18 = 6. The smallest is 6.

For grown-ups

Ideas to practise

  • Building numbers. Combine the place-value parts, including any zero places.
  • Place value. A digit has a different value in each position. Count the places from the right.
  • Comparing quantities. Compare the values, not the size or spacing of their pictures.
  • Addition and missing amounts. Combine the amounts, or work backwards from the total.
  • Factors and multiples. Factors divide an amount exactly; multiples are repeated totals. Choose which idea the situation needs.

A game mission has 8 untimed questions. Only the game saves choices and hints. A finished mission earns one launch charge and participation towards the Command bridge in Galaxy Command. The chapter goal is 8 different questions in finished sets; hints and wrong answers count as participation, not mastery. Some craft systems link more than one chapter.

Using the feedback

Learning reports distinguish hinted answers from independent first choices. They consider up to 20 recent different, unhinted questions per skill and level, and wait for at least five before suggesting extra practice. Repeating the same question does not add evidence. Reports are practice evidence, not IQ scores, diagnoses, ranks or predictions of competition results.

Ask the learner to explain a drawing or check with objects too. Choose Explore or an earlier chapter when a step feels too large.

Sources & limits

The grade topics use SOF IMO Class 5 published topic syllabus as their primary reference. The SOF sample and CREST previous-year paper below informed representations and reasoning demands. Providers have different topic boundaries; their syllabi are not interchangeable.

  • Sample, not an administered paper: SOF IMO Class 5 sample, 2026-27

No Olympiad provider is affiliated with or endorses Space Academy. This is not complete exam preparation; follow classroom teaching and check the current official syllabus too. Independent educator review is still needed for difficulty and breadth.

Content and coverage notes. To report a confusing question, describe the grade, chapter, level and question on the contact page. Do not send children’s personal information.
